# 10. Scripts reference

<!-- GENERATED by tools/gen_guide_docs.py from the --help of every command - do not edit by hand. -->

Every action is `scripts/ttctl <command>` (or the script in `scripts/` directly). Every command and subcommand
answers `--help`; this page is that output, regenerated in CI so it cannot drift. Global options and exit codes are
shown once, at the end of the first section.

## ttctl

```text
ttctl - install, run, stop and operate Team Tracker

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl [GLOBAL OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]        ttctl help COMMAND   (or: COMMAND --help)

INSTALL
  prereqs check|install [TOOL...]   detect and install prerequisites (user space first; asks before using root)
  setup [--with-db] [--install-missing] [--db native|docker|external] [--browsers] [--prod]
  doctor                            check tools, configuration, database and running processes

RUN (dev / UAT / single host)
  start [COMPONENT...]              server worker web (default) | gateway desktop slack
  stop  [COMPONENT...] [--with-db]  stop (default: everything that runs)
  restart [COMPONENT...]            stop + start
  status [--json]                   what runs, PIDs, ports, health
  logs [-f] [-n N] [COMPONENT...]   show / follow logs (.run/logs)
  run COMPONENT                     one component in the foreground (Ctrl-C stops it)

DATABASE
  db start|stop|status|create|migrate|seed|setup|reset|drop|backup|restore|psql|verify

AIR-GAPPED DELIVERY
  bundle create --target T [...]    on a connected machine: everything needed, in one file
  bundle info|verify FILE           show / check a bundle
  bundle install [FILE]             on the offline host (the bundle's ./install.sh does this)

DOCKER, CLIENT, BUILD
  docker up|down|stop|start|restart|ps|logs|seed|migrate|shell|psql|reset
  client install|uninstall|wheels|token|login|run|logout|status
  build [presentation|web|desktop|desktop-native|client|images|openapi]
  check [all|lint|typecheck|test|quick|e2e|fmt|ops]
  clean [--deps]

PRODUCTION (systemd, root)
  prod install --mode proxy|tls [--with-gateway] [--nginx]
  prod start|stop|restart|status|reload|logs|health|enable|disable|releases
  prod upgrade [GIT_REF] | prod upgrade --from-bundle FILE | prod rollback

REPOSITORY AND SUPPORT
  repo split --repo OWNER/NAME      publish internal plans to a private repo (docs/guide/14-repositories.md)
  repo purge-history                prepare (never run by default) a history rewrite
  repo secrets-scan [DIR]           committed secrets in files and history (gitleaks or detect-secrets)
  support-bundle [FILE]             logs + doctor + versions + masked config in one tar, to send out of a closed site
  version                           versions of ttctl, the app and the tools

EXAMPLES
  ttctl setup --with-db --install-missing
  ttctl -v start server
  ttctl bundle create --target rhel8-x86_64 --with-db rpm
  ttctl help db

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/README.md   (full guide)      docs/guide/10-scripts-reference.md   (every command's help)

GLOBAL OPTIONS (accepted anywhere, passed on to child scripts)
  -v, --verbose      print every command before it runs, every probe and the effective configuration (secrets masked)
  -vv, --trace       -v plus shell tracing (file:line of every command)
  -q, --quiet        only warnings and errors
  --dry-run          print what would run; change nothing
  -y, --yes          answer yes to every prompt (needed when there is no terminal)
  --no-color         plain output (also NO_COLOR=1)
  --log-file PATH    write the run log here instead of .run/logs/ttctl-<command>-<time>.log
  -h, --help         this help
  Environment: TT_VERBOSE=0|1|2  TT_QUIET=1  TT_DRY_RUN=1  TT_YES=1  TT_OFFLINE=1 (refuse network actions)

EXIT CODES
  0 ok   1 runtime failure   2 usage   3 prerequisite missing   4 blocked because offline   5 configuration
```

## prereqs

```text
ttctl prereqs - detect and install what Team Tracker needs

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl prereqs check [--json]
  ttctl prereqs install [TOOL...] [--user|--system] [--from-bundle DIR]

TOOLS
  user space (no root, into .tools/):  uv  python (3.12, uv-managed)  node (22.12.0)  pnpm (9.15.0)  chromium
  system packages (root):              postgresql (16 server + contrib)  psql (16 client)  curl  git  chromium-libs  docker
  Without TOOL, "install" installs every REQUIRED tool that is missing or too old.

OPTIONS
  --json              check: machine-readable output
  --user              install only user-space tools; print the commands for system packages instead of running them
  --system            also install system packages: shows the exact commands, asks first (or --yes), uses sudo when not root
  --from-bundle DIR   take the tools from an unpacked air-gapped bundle instead of the network
  TT_PG_SOURCE=module|pgdg   RHEL: PostgreSQL from the AppStream module stream postgresql:16 or from the PGDG repository
                             (default: the module when the host offers it)

SUPPORTED
  RHEL / Rocky / Alma 8 and 9, Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04, Debian 12 (x86_64); macOS for development only.

EXAMPLES
  ttctl prereqs check
  ttctl -v prereqs check --json
  ttctl prereqs install pnpm
  ttctl prereqs install postgresql --system --dry-run
  ttctl prereqs install --from-bundle /opt/tt-bundle

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/01-requirements.md   docs/guide/02-install-online.md
```

## setup

```text
ttctl setup - prerequisites, dependencies, configuration, builds (and the database)

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl setup [--with-db [--db native|docker|external] [--no-seed]] [--install-missing] [--browsers] [--prod]

STEPS
  1 prerequisites   checks the tools; offers to install missing user-space tools into .tools/ (no root)
  2 configuration   writes .env from .env.example if missing (never overwrites)
  3 Python          uv sync (offline: from the bundle's wheelhouse)
  4 web             pnpm install + builds the deck viewer (skipped when the bundle ships prebuilt apps)
  5 database        with --with-db: start, create, check the SERVER version and extensions, migrate, seed

OPTIONS
  --with-db           also prepare the database
  --db MODE           native (PostgreSQL 16 on this host, default) | docker (compose "db") | external (TT_DATABASE_URL)
  --no-seed           with --with-db: migrate but do not load the demo workspace
  --install-missing   install missing user-space tools without asking (system packages still ask, or need --yes)
  --browsers          also install Chromium for PDF/PNG export
  --prod              production flavour: no dev dependencies, random secrets in .env, web console built, no seed

  Without a terminal, missing tools are an error (exit 3) unless --install-missing or --yes is given.

EXAMPLES
  ttctl setup --with-db
  ttctl setup --with-db --install-missing --yes
  ttctl setup --with-db --db external
  ttctl -v setup --dry-run

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/02-install-online.md   docs/guide/03-install-airgapped.md
```

## start / run

```text
ttctl start - start components in the background (dev, UAT, single host)

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl start [COMPONENT...]
  ttctl run COMPONENT                 (= start --foreground: attached to the terminal, Ctrl-C stops it)

COMPONENTS
  server   API (uvicorn)             http://127.0.0.1:8000   (/docs, /healthz, /readyz)
  worker   background jobs (Procrastinate): daily logs, governance, recurrence, Jira, exports
  web      web console               http://localhost:5173  (Vite with Node; prebuilt apps/web/dist without Node)
  gateway  LLM gateway (tt-llm)      http://127.0.0.1:8700  (local models only unless TT_GATEWAY_MODE=config)
  desktop  desktop palette preview   http://localhost:1420  (needs Node)
  slack    Slack bot (needs SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_APP_TOKEN, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, TT_SLACK_LINK_SECRET)
  Default: server worker web. Each start waits for the health check and refuses a port that is already taken.

OPTIONS
  -f, --foreground   run one component attached to the terminal
  Settings: TT_HOST TT_PORT TT_WEB_PORT TT_GATEWAY_PORT TT_RELOAD TT_START_TIMEOUT TT_WEB_MODE=vite|static

FILES
  .run/<component>.pid    .run/logs/<component>.log

EXAMPLES
  ttctl start
  ttctl start server worker
  ttctl -v start gateway
  TT_PORT=9000 ttctl start server
  ttctl run server

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/04-run-and-stop.md
```

## db

```text
ttctl db - create, migrate, seed, back up and restore the PostgreSQL database

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl db SUBCOMMAND [ARGS] [--db native|docker|external]

SUBCOMMANDS
  start | stop        start/stop the database service (native: systemd/service/pg_ctl/Homebrew; docker: the compose "db"
                      container; external: nothing to do)
  status              server reachable? SERVER version (SHOW server_version_num), extensions, migration revision
  check               like status, but exits non-zero with an explanation when something is wrong
  create              role + database from TT_DATABASE_URL and the extensions pg_trgm ltree btree_gist (needs a superuser:
                      sudo -u postgres locally, or TT_DB_ADMIN_URL for a remote server)
  migrate             alembic upgrade head + job-queue schema (tt-admin migrate)
  seed [--reset]      demo workspace "acme"
  setup               start + create + check + migrate + seed
  reset | drop        destructive; asks first (--yes to skip); refuses while server/worker run
  backup [FILE]       pg_dump -Fc (default backups/tt-<time>.dump)
  restore FILE        replace the database with a dump
  psql [ARGS]         SQL shell on the app database
  verify [WORKSPACE]  event log vs tables (tt-admin verify-projection), default acme

DATABASE MODES (--db, or TT_DB_MODE in .env)
  native     PostgreSQL 16 installed on this host (ttctl prereqs install postgresql --system)
  docker     the "db" service of docker-compose.yml (postgres:16)
  external   a server you run elsewhere; TT_DATABASE_URL points at it; TT_DB_ADMIN_URL lets "create" make the role/db

CLIENT VERSION
  Only backup, restore and psql use a client program, and it must be >= the server (16). An older system psql
  (e.g. 10 on RHEL 8) is fine for everything else; these three then use .tools/pgsql, /usr/pgsql-16 or the
  postgres:16 container, in that order.

EXAMPLES
  ttctl db setup
  ttctl db status --db external
  ttctl db backup /var/backups/tt/before-upgrade.dump
  ttctl --yes db restore backups/tt-20261114-0900.dump
  ttctl db psql -c 'select count(*) from work_items'

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/05-database.md
```

## bundle

```text
ttctl bundle - air-gapped delivery in two steps

SYNOPSIS
  Step A, on a connected machine with Docker:
    ttctl bundle create --target TARGET [--with-db rpm|deb|image] [--with-browsers] [--with-llm MODEL]
                           [--with-docker-images] [--with-dev] [--out DIR] [--compress zst|gz] [--sign GPG_KEY]
  Step B, on the air-gapped host (after copying the file):
    tar -xf tt-bundle-VERSION-TARGET.tar.zst && cd tt-bundle-VERSION-TARGET && ./install.sh [OPTIONS]
    (= ttctl bundle install [FILE|--from-dir DIR] [--prefix DIR] [--with-db] [--mode dev|prod])
  Anywhere:
    ttctl bundle info FILE        show the manifest (versions, target, components, sizes)
    ttctl bundle verify FILE      check every file against SHA256SUMS (and the signature when present)

TARGETS
  rhel8-x86_64 rhel9-x86_64 ubuntu22.04-amd64 ubuntu24.04-amd64
  The bundle is built inside a container of the target OS, so every binary matches its glibc and package set.

CREATE OPTIONS
  --with-db rpm|deb    PostgreSQL 16 server, contrib and client packages with all dependencies (rpm for rhel*, deb for ubuntu*)
  --with-db image      the postgres:16 Docker image instead (host runs --db docker)
  --with-browsers      Chromium + its system library packages (PDF/PNG export of decks)
  --browsers-from DIR  copy Chromium from an existing Playwright browser directory instead of downloading it
  --with-llm MODEL     Ollama + MODEL for the LLM gateway (local_only); without it the app uses the deterministic parser
  --with-docker-images docker save tars of team-tracker-server, team-tracker-llm-gateway and postgres:16
  --with-dev           Node, pnpm and an offline pnpm store, dev Python wheels (to rebuild and test on the host)
  --out DIR            output directory (default dist/)       --compress zst|gz   (default zst; gz for hosts without zstd)
  --sign KEY           detached GPG signature of SHA256SUMS   --allow-dirty       include uncommitted changes
  Always included: source of the commit, uv, Python 3.12, a hash-pinned wheelhouse of every locked
  dependency + the workspace wheels, the PREBUILT web console and deck viewer (no Node on the server), the client kit
  (tt for Linux/macOS/Windows), docs/guide and scripts/.

INSTALL OPTIONS
  --prefix DIR     where releases go (default /opt/team-tracker as root, ~/team-tracker otherwise): DIR/releases/VERSION, DIR/current
  --with-db        install the bundled PostgreSQL packages (root; asks first) or load the image
  --mode dev|prod  dev: ready for "ttctl db setup" + "ttctl start"; prod: also "ttctl prod install" (systemd, root)
  --force          install although the bundle was built for another OS
  The install verifies checksums first, then uses only the bundle. It writes TT_OFFLINE=1 (and UV_OFFLINE, PIP_NO_INDEX,
  npm_config_offline, COREPACK_ENABLE_NETWORK=0, PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD) to .ttctl.env: from then on every
  ttctl action that would need the network stops with exit 4 and names the missing bundle option.

EXAMPLES
  ttctl bundle create --target rhel8-x86_64 --with-db rpm --with-browsers
  ttctl bundle create --target ubuntu24.04-amd64 --with-db deb --compress gz
  ttctl bundle verify dist/tt-bundle-1.0.0-rhel8-x86_64.tar.zst
  ./install.sh --with-db --mode prod

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/03-install-airgapped.md   docs/guide/07-upgrade-and-rollback.md
```

SYNOPSIS

  ttctl docker logs [-f] [SERVICE] | seed [--reset] | migrate | shell [SERVICE] | psql | reset

OPTIONS

  Offline hosts: load the images first (bundle install does it when the bundle has --with-docker-images).

## client

```text
ttctl client - install and use the "tt" command line

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl client install | uninstall | status
  ttctl client wheels [DIR]               installable wheels (tt-cli + its two libraries), default dist/client
  ttctl client token [@handle] [ws]       DEV ONLY: mint an API token (Development sign-in)
  ttctl client login [@handle] [ws]       DEV ONLY: mint a token and run "tt login" against this server
  ttctl client run ARGS...                run tt from the repository without installing it
  ttctl client logout                     delete the stored client configuration (keeps the outbox)

  On a user's machine without this repository (or offline) use the client kit instead:
    Linux/macOS:  ./install.sh install        Windows:  .\install.ps1 install      (docs/guide/08-clients.md)

EXAMPLES
  ttctl client install
  ttctl client login @sara
  ttctl client run say "fixed the login loop, took 2h" --yes
  ttctl client wheels dist/client

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/08-clients.md
```

## prod (service control)

```text
ttctl prod - control the production services (systemd units tt-server, tt-worker, tt-llm-gateway)

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl prod start | stop | restart | status | enable | disable
  ttctl prod reload                 re-read TLS certificates without dropping connections (tls mode)
  ttctl prod logs [-f] [UNIT]       journalctl for the units (default: all)
  ttctl prod health [URL]           GET /readyz (http://127.0.0.1:8000, or https://127.0.0.1:8443 in tls mode)
  ttctl prod install ...            see: ttctl help prod install
  ttctl prod upgrade | rollback | releases   see: ttctl help prod upgrade

EXAMPLES
  ttctl prod status
  sudo ttctl prod restart
  ttctl prod logs -f tt-worker
  ttctl prod health

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/06-production.md
```

## prod install

```text
ttctl prod install - production install on one Linux host with systemd (run as root)

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl prod install --mode proxy|tls [--prefix DIR] [--with-gateway] [--nginx] [--no-start]

MODES
  proxy   API on 127.0.0.1:8000 behind nginx/Caddy that terminates HTTPS (recommended)
  tls     API serves HTTPS itself on :8443 from PEM files in /etc/tt/tls (+ :8080 redirect); see docs/guide/06-production.md#tls

OPTIONS
  --prefix DIR     a bundle install's prefix (units then run DIR/current, so upgrades and rollbacks switch one symlink)
  --with-gateway   also the LLM gateway service (privacy_mode local_only when the host is offline)
  --nginx          install deploy/nginx/team-tracker.conf into /etc/nginx/conf.d (edit server_name and certificates)
  --no-start       install and enable, do not start

WHAT IT DOES
  system user "tt"; /etc/tt, /var/lib/team-tracker; dependencies (online: uv sync --no-dev + web build; offline: already
  installed by the bundle); /etc/tt/tt.env with random secrets if missing; systemd units tt-server, tt-worker
  (tt-llm-gateway); migrations; start. Idempotent: run it again after changing /etc/tt/tt.env.

EXAMPLES
  sudo ttctl prod install --mode proxy --nginx
  sudo ttctl prod install --mode tls
  sudo ttctl --dry-run prod install --mode proxy
  sudo /opt/team-tracker/current/scripts/ttctl prod install --mode proxy --prefix /opt/team-tracker

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/06-production.md   docs/guide/07-upgrade-and-rollback.md
```

## prod upgrade / rollback / releases

```text
ttctl prod upgrade / rollback / releases - upgrade with a backup first, roll back to the previous release

SYNOPSIS
  sudo ttctl prod upgrade [GIT_REF] [--no-backup]          online: git checkout, deps, build, migrate, restart
  sudo ttctl prod upgrade --from-bundle FILE [--no-backup] offline: new release dir from the bundle, migrate, switch
  sudo ttctl prod rollback                                 back to the previous release (or the previous commit)
  ttctl prod releases                                      list installed releases (bundle installs)

HOW
  1 backup the database (/var/backups/tt)   2 install the new code next to the running one
  3 migrate (migrations are additive: the old code still runs on the new schema)
  4 switch (bundle: the PREFIX/current symlink; git: the checkout) and restart   5 health check
  If the health check fails, the previous release is switched back and restarted automatically (exit 1, TT-E301).

EXAMPLES
  sudo ttctl prod upgrade v1.1.0
  sudo /opt/team-tracker/current/scripts/ttctl prod upgrade --from-bundle /media/usb/tt-bundle-1.1.0-rhel8-x86_64.tar.zst
  sudo ttctl prod rollback
  ttctl prod releases

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/07-upgrade-and-rollback.md
```

## repo split

```text
ttctl repo split - publish plans, reviews, decisions and design material to a private, protected repository

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl repo split --repo OWNER/NAME [--history] [--from REF] [--no-protect] [--no-scan] [--dry-run]

WHAT
  The paths in scripts/repo/internal-paths.txt are copied - each from the last commit that still had it - into a new
  repository, together with an overlay (README explaining the layout, CODEOWNERS, the handover tool adapted to read
  the product checkout from TT_PRODUCT_DIR). Then a secrets scan runs over the result. Only then the repository is
  created PRIVATE (an existing one must already be private), main is pushed and protected: pull request with one
  approval, no force-push, no deletion.

OPTIONS
  --repo OWNER/NAME  target (e.g. mdaoor/team_tracker-internal)
  --history          keep the full git history of those paths (needs git-filter-repo); default: one snapshot commit
  --from REF         take every path from this commit instead
  --no-protect       skip branch protection         --no-scan    skip the secrets scan (not recommended)
  --dry-run          build it locally in .run/internal-repo and stop: nothing is created or pushed
  Needs: git; for publishing, the GitHub CLI signed in with rights to create repositories (gh auth login).
  Removing files from the product repository does not remove them from its history: see
  ttctl help repo purge-history and docs/guide/14-repositories.md#history.

EXAMPLES
  ttctl repo split --repo mdaoor/team_tracker-internal --history --dry-run
  ttctl repo split --repo mdaoor/team_tracker-internal --history
  ttctl repo split --repo mdaoor/team_tracker-internal --from 31222e5

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/14-repositories.md
```

## repo purge-history

```text
ttctl repo purge-history - report, and only on explicit request perform, removing the internal paths from ALL history

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl repo purge-history                                  report only (default): what a rewrite would change
  ttctl repo purge-history --i-understand-this-rewrites-public-history
                                                                rewrite a MIRROR clone in .run/purge-mirror; push nothing
  (pushing is a separate, manual step printed at the end - this script never force-pushes)

WHY THIS IS NOT AUTOMATIC
  Removing files from the tip leaves them in every older commit, every branch and every merged pull request. A rewrite
  changes every commit id: every clone, fork and open pull request breaks, and GitHub keeps the old pull request refs
  (refs/pull/*) and cached views until GitHub Support purges them. Choose between the three options in
  docs/guide/14-repositories.md#history before running anything; the recommended one does not need this script.

REPORT
  the internal paths (scripts/repo/internal-paths.txt), how many commits and which branches and pull-request refs
  contain them, and the exact commands of the rewrite.

EXAMPLES
  ttctl repo purge-history
  ttctl -v repo purge-history
  ttctl repo purge-history --i-understand-this-rewrites-public-history

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/14-repositories.md#history
```

## repo secrets-scan

```text
ttctl repo secrets-scan - look for committed secrets in a repository's files and history

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl repo secrets-scan [REPO_DIR] [--report FILE]

HOW
  gitleaks when installed (gitleaks detect --log-opts=--all); otherwise detect-secrets (from PyPI, via uvx) over the
  working tree and over every patch in the history (git log -p --all). Findings print with file, line/commit and type;
  the exit code is 1 when anything was found. Known test fixtures (dev passwords "tt", dummy tokens in tests) are
  reported too: review them, they are not ignored silently.

EXAMPLES
  ttctl repo secrets-scan
  ttctl repo secrets-scan .run/internal-repo --report .run/secrets-internal.json
  ttctl -v repo secrets-scan /path/to/another/checkout

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/14-repositories.md#secrets-scan
```

## support-bundle

```text
ttctl support-bundle - logs, doctor output, versions and the MASKED configuration in one file

SYNOPSIS
  ttctl support-bundle [FILE] [--days N]

CONTENTS
  versions.txt (ttctl version), doctor.txt, prereqs.json, status.json, config.txt (TT_* settings with secrets and
  database passwords replaced by ***), the component and ttctl run logs of the last N days (default 3),
  bundle manifest.json when installed from a bundle, systemd unit status and the last 500 journal lines in production.
  Not included: .env itself, the database, uploaded files, anything under /etc/tt except unit status.
  Review the file before sending it: logs can contain work item titles.

OPTIONS
  FILE       output (default .run/tt-support-<host>-<time>.tar.gz)
  --days N   how many days of logs (default 3)

EXAMPLES
  ttctl support-bundle
  ttctl support-bundle /media/usb/tt-support.tar.gz
  ttctl support-bundle --days 14

SEE ALSO
  docs/guide/11-troubleshooting.md
```

## version

```text
ttctl version   - versions of ttctl, the app (VERSION file or git), the OS and every tool
```
